slides.notes:
The key improvement over Review 1 is fairness of the no-pheromone comparison. Previously we hid channels only after training a full-input policy, which creates an unfamiliar input distribution. Here a different PPO model learns from masked inputs throughout training and is evaluated the same way. It still sees food presence, nest, occupancy, boundaries and its own carrying/progress. Both policies have the same shared thirty-two-by-thirty-two actor and local critic. The random reference is a non-learned check. We require a strict stochastic delivery advantage in every declared seed, not just a favorable average or one lucky run.

The failed candidates are part of the evidence. We initially tested search distance and repeat trips, then simplified layouts. Slower evaporation increased the frequency of visible food pheromone but did not guarantee a performance advantage, so visibility alone was not sufficient. Candidate G was close: the full policy finished faster but tied the no-pheromone model at the maximum delivery count for seed seven. The predeclared strict gate correctly rejected that tie. Shortening the deadline did not reveal a reliable advantage because learning became unstable, even with more training. Candidate J returned to the stable long horizon and changed only capacity.

slides.notes:
Candidate J retains Candidate G’s grid, four-agent population, distant adjacent cluster, long horizon and slower evaporation. Only food capacity changes, from thirty to fifty per patch, raising the maximum score from sixty to one hundred. This tests the documented ceiling explanation without changing policy architecture, reward or observations. Map seeds vary the cluster location, reducing the value of memorizing a single fixed route. There are no obstacles or diffusion in this calibration. Each PPO job requests three hundred thousand agent transitions and uses the same optimizer settings. This is a clean task, so there is no attacker fraction to report for Candidate J’s Phase 2A result.
